subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should memory_search use a non-zero periodic sync fallback by default when watcher events may be missed, or should periodic sync remain opt-in with a narrower watcher-health repair?
rationale: The core bug is valid, but the likely fix changes a shipped default/fallback behavior and can add background indexing work for existing users, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Default fallback with opt-out
options.body: Set a non-zero default interval, force dirty rescan on interval ticks, preserve explicit `intervalMinutes: 0`, and require upgrade/runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Keep interval opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at `0` and fix only watcher error/health diagnostics, avoiding new background indexing for existing users but leaving less automatic recovery.

options.title: Adopt a replacement fix
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting linked PR and sponsor a narrow replacement that keeps the same behavior decision explicit in the PR body.

recommendation.title: Default fallback with opt-out
recommendation.body: Set a non-zero default interval, force dirty rescan on interval ticks, preserve explicit `intervalMinutes: 0`, and require upgrade/runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal for memory search and the memory engine boundary involved in this default/fallback decision.
